title: 《高等微積分》第 47 集｜反映射定理｜Loomis & Sternberg 第 3 章 §11
description:
本集是 Loomis 與 Sternberg《Advanced Calculus》第 3 章第 11 節「隱函數定理」的中段（書頁 166 到 167）。

上一集的定理 11.1 假設隱函數已經存在。定理 11.2 反過來製造它：空間完備、G 連續可微、G 在某一點等於零、而且第二個偏微分在那一點可逆，那麼在 α 附近有一顆球，球上存在唯一一個連續可微的 F 滿足那個恆等式，而且自動滿足 F(α) 等於 β。有限維一定完備，所以在實數的 n 維空間上那個假設是白得的；證明要用第 4 章的不動點定理。

「唯一」是局部的。影片用 η 平方等於 ξ 示範：同一個 ξ 有正負兩個解，指定 β 就選定了一支，定理保證的是那顆小球上只有那一支，不是整條曲線上唯一。在原點兩支黏在一起，第二個偏微分等於零，定理不適用——而那裡確實沒有單值的解。所以可逆不是技術性的裝飾，它剛好排除掉分支交會的地方。

結論裡的 F 不只可微、還連續可微，這是白得的：公式裡出現的每一樣東西都連續，而且取反元素在算子範數下也連續。同一個理由還給出另一件事——可逆是一個開條件，所以一點可逆就代表附近整片都可逆，一點的假設撐出一整片的結論。

定理 11.3 是它的特例，可是有自己的名字：反映射定理。H 連續可微、微分在 β 可逆，那麼 H 在 β 附近可逆，反函數也連續可微。證明只有一行：令 G 等於 ξ 減 H 作用在 η 上，它對第二個變數的偏微分就是負的 dH，可逆，隱函數定理直接套上去，交出來的 F 滿足 H 接上 F 等於恆等映射。推論給出大家熟悉的說法：β 有一個開鄰域使 H 在上面是單射，它的像是開集，反函數在那個開集上連續可微。

每一句都是局部的。影片最後用複數平方那個映射說明：它在每個非原點的地方都局部可逆，可是全域不是單射，兩個相反的點有同一個像。局部反函數是用牛頓法逼出來的，它的雅可比矩陣算出來正好是原矩陣的反矩陣。

title: Advanced Calculus, Episode 47 | The Inverse Mapping Theorem | Ch. 3, §11
description:
This episode is the middle part of section 11 of chapter 3, The Implicit Function Theorem, pages 166 to 167 of Loomis and Sternberg's Advanced Calculus.

Theorem 11.1 assumed the implicit function already existed. Theorem 11.2 produces it: if the spaces are complete, G is continuously differentiable, G vanishes at a point, and the second partial differential inverts there, then a ball about alpha carries a unique continuously differentiable F satisfying the identity, and it automatically satisfies F of alpha equals beta. Finite dimensional spaces are complete, so in real n-space that hypothesis is free; the proof needs the fixed point theorem of chapter four.

Unique means locally unique. Eta squared equals xi shows what that costs: the same xi has two solutions, naming beta picks one branch, and the theorem promises only that branch on the small ball, not along the whole curve. At the origin the branches join, the second partial differential vanishes, and the theorem is silent — and there genuinely is no single valued solution there. Invertibility is no decoration: it excludes exactly where branches meet.

The F in the conclusion is continuously differentiable and not merely differentiable, and that comes free: everything appearing in the formula is continuous, and taking an inverse is continuous in the operator norm. The same fact gives something else — invertibility is an open condition, so inverting at one point means inverting on a whole patch, and an assumption at one point buys a conclusion on a neighborhood.

Theorem 11.3 is a special case with a name of its own: the inverse mapping theorem. If H is continuously differentiable with invertible differential at beta, then H is invertible near beta and the inverse is continuously differentiable too. The proof takes one line: let G be xi minus H of eta, whose partial differential in the second variable is minus dH and therefore inverts, apply the implicit function theorem, and the F it hands back satisfies H after F equals the identity. The corollary is the familiar wording: beta has an open neighborhood on which H is injective, its image is open, and the inverse is continuously differentiable there.

Every clause is local. The closing example is the complex squaring map: locally invertible everywhere but the origin, yet globally injective nowhere, since two opposite points share an image. Its local inverse is reached by Newton's method here, and the Jacobian matrix that comes out is the inverse of the original's.
